articleTitle: Tunable microstrip patch antenna based on liquid crystals
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this project a novel design of a compact rectangular microstrip patch antenna using Liquid Crystals Substrates (LCs) for microwave applications is presented. To benefit from liquid crystal anisotropy and thus obtain frequency agility, a low bias voltage of about 10V is applied. This technique is used to 4 LCs with DC voltage satisfies a minimal return loss of -52.47dB with a bandwidth of 60MHz for operating frequency of 2.53GHz. The variation of the simulation resonance frequency (ΔFr) obtained after applying a continuous voltage is 530MHz corresponding to an important frequency agility of 26.5%. This method based on LCs can be used to cover several frequency bands, overcome the problem of narrow bandwidth of antenna, increase the peak gain and achieved a good return loss. The design and simulation of antenna is done by using Ansoft HFSS.13. The simulated results are compared with experimental data, and good agreement is obtained.

articleTitle: Asymptotic models of weakly filled PFSG
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic wave's scattering by pre-fractal strips' gratings (PFSG) is formulated in the classically rigorous form on the base of the integral equation technique. Considerable attention is focused on asymptotic models of weakly filled PFSG, which have explicit solutions. Scattered fields in the far-zone are considered in details. Two calculation algorithms have been developed for direction patterns and computer simulations have been performed.

articleTitle: Solution of the direct problem of electromagnetic waves propagation in foams
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Model of water foam presented from 7 layers with different dielectric characteristics for thickness 5, 10 and 15 mm. Calculations were made in microwave band of 8-12 GHz. Layers have value of foaming ratio from 6 till 350. The results of reflection and transmission characteristics show dependence from thickness of layers in range of 5-15 mm.

articleTitle: UXO classification procedures applied to advanced EMI sensors and models
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Unexploded Ordnances (UXO) classification procedure consists of the following: background subtractions, data inversions and targets feature parameters estimations, and separating UXO from non-hazardous anomalies. First, each dataset is normalized by a corresponding Tx-current; then, all data files are background subtracted; third, the background corrected data are inverted and targets intrinsic (effective polarizabilities) and extrinsic (locations) are extracted; next, the extracted intrinsic and extrinsic parameters are used for generating prioritized and training targets lists; Finally, once the ground truth for training targets are provided, then prioritized targets are reclassified and final dig list is created. In this paper, the detailed steps of UXO classification procedure using the advanced EMI sensors and models are presented along with the processing and analysis approaches that are used to generate a prioritized dig list.

articleTitle: SH-wave scattering by plane low contrast piezoelectric inclusion
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Scattering of (antiplane) harmonic SH-waves by a linear piezoelectric inclusion in an elastic medium is considered. Components of the presented composite are under conditions of longitudinal shear. The thickness of the inclusion is much smaller than its length. Wave fields scattered into the far zone (Fraunhofer zone) are investigated combining matched asymptotic expansions and the boundary integral equation method. The influence of mechanical and geometric parameters of composite on the amplitude-frequency characteristics of SH-waves is analyzed.

articleTitle: Directivity of thin antennas
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The analytical expressions are obtained, and the method of calculating directional patterns of thin antennas with large dimensions was proposed. Directivity of dipoles, V-dipoles and in-phase radiators of similar types were calculated. The importance of accounting the magnitude PF for the estimate of a communication range was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Active sources localization by measured field
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this article there is considered a new approach for Active Sources Localization (ASL) based on the measured or given data of the field's distribution on some surface. The task belongs to the solution of the inverse scattering problem based on the Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS). Inherently, proposed approach is using fundamental property of the scattered field — the uniqueness of the wave field's analytical continuation along and backwards its propagation. In the paper we discuss about two approaches for solution state problem. The positions of the active source are determined by means of the converging and diverging wave's function. The program package is created based on both approach and the numerical experiments are realized. The results of simulation show the efficiency of this new proposal.

articleTitle: Detection of conductivity voids and landmines using high frequency electromagnetic induction
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Electromagnetic induction (EMI) instruments have been traditionally used to detect high electric conductivity discrete targets such as metal unexploded ordnance (UXO). The frequencies used for this EMI regime have typically been less than 100 kHz. To detect intermediate conductivity objects like carbon fiber, even less conductive saturated salts, and even voids embedded in conducting soils, higher frequencies up to the low megahertz range are required in order to capture characteristic relaxation responses. In this context, nonconducting lastic landmines can be considered a void plus small metallic parts such as the firing pin. To predict EMI phenomena at frequencies up to 15MHz, we modeled the response of conducting and nonconducting targets using the the Method of Auxiliary Sources. Our high-frequency electromagnetic induction (HFEMI) instrument is able to acquire EMI data at frequencies up to that same high limit. Modeled and measured characteristic relaxation signatures compare favorably and indicate new sensing possibilities in a variety of scenarios including the detection of voids and landmines.

articleTitle: Scattering of H-polarized electromagnetic wave by grooved dihedral wedge co-axially coupled with dielectric covered metal slotted cylinder
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Scattering of electromagnetic wave is considered for a composite structure consisting of a conducting dihedral wedge with four grooves and that is co-axially coupled with a slotted cylinder covered with dielectric. The boundary-value method is employed using completeness property of the angular functions in the respective intervals. Problem is reduced to solution of system of algebraic equations of second kind for the unknown coefficients of Fourier expansion of scattered field. Analytical solution is obtained for certain values of cylinder slot-width and electrical radius of cylinder. Scattered far-field and backscatter radar cross section (BRCS) of the structure are formulated.

articleTitle: The optimal size directive gain antenna creation
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper presents creation of the optimal size directive gain antenna which radiates a desired predefined pattern. Theory of this study based on the Method of the Auxiliary Sources (MAS) was published in previous paper and briefly reminding the basic ideas of the approach results of the experimental measurements on created real prototype antenna are discussed. In practice during the antenna syntheses and its design very crucial problem is to minimize the size if the aperture which depends on the directive gain. We introduce the volume antenna which could minimize diameter of the aperture. Comparatively easy to construct and simply for feeding system with another positive radiations qualities like minimal side lobes and reactive fields makes interesting to use offered methodology. Eventually, for predicted antenna geometry using the MAS together with real experiments additionally to verify validity and correctness of approach the EMC Studio simulation used. All results are in a good agreement.

articleTitle: Predicting Earth magnetic anomalies from measured EMAG2 data
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Magnetic anomaly maps are important for scientific and practical applications; such as they provide insight into the subsurface structure and composition of the Earth's terrestrial and oceanic crusts. These maps are widely applicable for geological exploration and detection of man-made subsurface anomalies. There is available high-resolution 2 arc-minute global Earth Magnetic Anomaly Grid data (EMAG2) at 4 km above the geoid [1], which has been created using various satellite, ship, and airborne magnetic measurements. However, many. if not all. practical applications require EMAG data at different elevations and different resolutions. To achieve this demand here EMAG2 data at 4 km elevation is remapped at different elevations and resolutions using the method of auxiliary sources. Comparisons between predicted and measured data are demonstrated.

articleTitle: EM exposure study on an inhomogeneous human model considering different hand positions
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The main aim and the novelty of the proposed research is to study Mobile phone EM exposure thermal influence for the inhomogeneous woman models in case of different hand (finger) positions, holding the mobile phone, at 900 MHz, 1900 MHz and 3700 MHz frequencies. The motivation of this work is the necessity to consider influence of the hand, its position and position of the handset upon the near field for proper understanding of the exposure nature. Numerical simulations are carried out using finite-difference time domain (FDTD) method to estimate the specific absorption rate (SAR) and temperature rise caused by absorption of EM field energy in the human tissues. The obtained results are presented and analyzed below.

articleTitle: Numerical approach for determination of scatterer form on the scattering amplitude
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The numerical approach to determine the shape of scattering body by the known scattering amplitude has been developed. The inverse scattering problem is formulated for 3-D case. The system of equations regarding the function describing form of body and normal derivative of field on the body is derived. The system is ill-posed because of equation for finding the form of body shape. The specification for 2D case is considered in details. The numerical algorithm for solving the obtained system is elaborated.

articleTitle: Modeling of anisotropic magneto-piezoelastic materials
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The anisotropic magneto-piezoelastic materials are analyzed. It is shown that Green's function method is applicable to time harmonic magneto-elastic-piezoelectricity problems using the boundary integral technique, and the exact analytical solutions are obtained. As an application, a two-dimensional static plane-strain problem is considered to investigate the effect of magnetic field on piezoelectric materials. The closed-form analytical solutions are obtained for a number of boundary conditions for all components of the magneto-piezoelectric field. As a special case, analytical results are presented for two-dimensional static magneto-electroelastic field of a piezoelectric solid subjected to a concentrated line load and an electric charge.

articleTitle: Cumulative stimulated echo in magnets
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The results of the cumulative NMR stimulated echo phenomenon study in lithium ferrite are presented. This echo is generated by the joint action of a train of weak writing radio-frequency pulses and final reading radio-frequency pulse which exhibits the growth of intensity at increasing the number of exciting radio-frequency pulses. Similar effect was earlier observed for the case of cumulative stimulated photon echo.

articleTitle: Transparent cubically polarizable media with layered or periodic structures
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The work deals with layered or periodic nonlinear media. For such structures, a condition of phase synchronism of the scattered and generated oscillations is formulated. Results of numerical experiments for the case of absolutely transparent (in the linear approximation) cubically polarizable layered media are explained.

articleTitle: Influence of a dielectric insert on energy characteristics of a cruciform waveguide junction
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The energy characteristics of the junction consisting of two perpendicular crossed infinite rectangular waveguides coupling through a narrow slot are studied. A transverse slot cut in the wide wall of the first waveguide coincides with the similar slot orientated along a longitudinal axis of the second waveguide. A dielectric insert is allocated in the coupling slot of the first waveguide. The geometry of the joint ensures the evanescent mode of the first waveguide operation. A possibility to vary the power transmission coefficient between the waveguides over a wide range by varying the slot length and electrical parameters of the insert is shown.

articleTitle: Stability of the solutions to synthesis problems of radiating systems according to power radiation pattern
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The nonlinear synthesis problems of radiating systems with use of energy criterion is considered. Stability of the approximate pseudosolutions with respect to the right part of the equation errors are proved.

articleTitle: Resonant phenomena at diffraction of tilted impedance dipole field on finite size screen
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The 3D radiation patterns of the tilted impedance wire dipole located over a perfectly conducting infinitely thin finite size screen are investigated by the uniform geometric diffraction theory method. The technique is developed for definition of a slope angle of the wire dipole taking into account the diffraction effects on the screen edges at which the circularly polarized wave in the set directions of the main observation planes in the far zone is radiated. The extremely achievable field amplitude of the circularly polarized wave in the certain angles of the main observation planes as well as the appropriate dipole's slope angles depending on the square screen sizes are defined. It is shown that the resonant phenomena take place on account of diffraction effects on screen edges. At certain dipole's spacing the radiation intensity in case of exiting screen by a resonant impedance dipole more than twice exceeds intensity in case of exiting screen by ideally conducting dipole with the same length.

articleTitle: Interaction of transition radiation of charged particle with periodically modulated anisotropic magnetodielectric filling of the waveguide
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Interaction of transition radiation of a charged particle with periodically modulated anisotropic magnetodielectric filling of the regular waveguide is considered. It is assumed, that the charged particle moves perpendicular to the waveguide axis with constant velocity. The analytical expressions for the transverse-magnetic (TM) field in the first approximation relative to the modulation indexes of filling are found. The energy of transition radiation in the region of “weak” (not resonant) interaction between the radiation wave and the modulated filling is calculated in the case of rectangular waveguide. Modulated filling of the waveguide leads to the fact that the TM field in the waveguide represents a set of space harmonics with different amplitudes. In the expression for the energy of transition radiation of the charged particle unlike the case of the unmodulated filling is added the member proportional to the modulation index of the first degree.

articleTitle: Absorption spectroscopy of silver atoms and nanomolecular studies of DNA and some organic structures
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The goal of present research is the absorption-spectroscopic studies of resonance interaction of silver atoms in different conditions: 1. In silver nanoparticle; 2. Bound to double helix of DNA; 3. In complex with oligodeoxynucleotides (dodecamer d(CGCGAATTCGCG)); 4. Incapsulated in polyamidoamine (PAMAM) of fourth generation G4 (~4 nm); 5. Absorbed by cellophane membrane. It is shown that AgNPs represent liquid drops which moisture the DNA surface at interaction. At photo-irradiation of AgNPs - DNA complex DNA dependant conformational transition takes place due to fast and intensive heating. It is shown also that in the interaction of atoms of silver reduced by ascorbic acid and in photo - desorption of AgNPs DNA double helix serves as a matrix, namely together with the silver atoms forms the rigid one-dimensional periodic structure.

articleTitle: Structure of phase-asymmetric solutions of circular antenna synthesis problem by amplitude radiation pattern with axially independent data
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The synthesis problem by the amplitude radiation pattern is considered for the circular aperture antennas. The prescribed pattern is assumed to be axially-symmetric. The solutions with asymmetric phase patterns are analyzed numerically.

articleTitle: Application of the method of auxiliary sources for the spherical and ellipsoid resonators
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In the previous work [1] there was shown the efficient application of the Method of auxiliary sources (MAS) for the problems of Eigen frequencies and electromagnetic resonator's Eigen Fields. The calculations for numerical results were conducted for 2D case, when the resonator is bounded by the cylindrical surface. There was shown the efficiency of the proposed method in comparison to the traditional method, based on the numerical solution of the linear algebraic equations homogenous system. In the given work there is considered the 3D case with the examples of the spherical and elliptical resonators. There is investigated the error of the solution and the boundary condition satisfaction. The short description of the corresponding theory is given below. After that there is considered some numerical results of volume resonators' excitation in order to determine their Eigen frequencies and Eigen fields.

articleTitle: A hybrid NFS approach for modeling of complicated antenna problems
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper presents a novel near-field-source (NFS) approach for modeling of antenna problems on complex geometries, when knowing fields radiated from antenna mounted only on a small part of geometry. This problem is reduced to a hybrid antenna problem for equivalent currents on imaginary surrounding surface, when given the fields on the remote surface and implying boundary conditions on the adjoined surface. The suggested hybrid NFS approach is validated on monopole antenna problem mounted on plate geometry. Then it is applied to car geometry with monopole antenna. A good agreement between the results for original and NFS antenna geometries is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Determination of biconical cavity eigenfrequencies using fractional-rational approximation of its response obtained as solution of excitation problem
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The solution of the excitation problem for the biconical cavity analysis by overlapping domain decomposition in combination with the collocation method has been examined. For determination of eigenfrequencies, the fractional-rational approximation of the cavity frequency response with its excitation has been used. Using the proposed approach the cone angle dependence of the eigenfrequencies of the azimuthal-symmetric oscillations of the biconical cavity has been obtained.

articleTitle: Fast fields calculation using adaptive cross approximation
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: When the number of field observation points and number of Method of Moments (MoM) currents are large, calculation of scattered electric and magnetic fields requires significant time. In this paper we demonstrate usage of Adaptive Cross Approximation (ACA) to speed up calculation of scattered field, formulated like scattering matrix multiplication on currents vector. To demonstrate efficiency of described technique, it is implemented in two different MoM solvers and applied to human exposure problems with the large number of field observation points. A good agreement between the results, obtained using direct and fast field calculations is demonstrated.

articleTitle: About the branching of real solutions of the second type in synthesis problems of radiating systems with a flat aperture
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A synthesis problem of the radiating system with flat aperture by given requirements to the amplitude directivity pattern is considered. Nonuniqueness and branching of solutions depending on two real parameters and the properties of a given amplitude DP are characteristic features of this class of problems. The equation to find a set of branching points of real solutions of three types is obtained. Algorithms and examples of finding the optimal solutions are given.

articleTitle: Lightwave amplification in carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper, we have investigated the possibility of terahertz (THz) amplification in zigzag carbon nanotube (ZCNT). The semiclassical Boltzmann transport equation with a constant relaxation time has been used for a ZCNT under simultaneous AC and DC bias fields. The I-V curve with negative differential conductivity (NDC) has been illustrated for this structure. THz amplification can be deduced in the region that the NDC has been occurred. The impact of angular frequencies and diameters of ZCNT on NDC have also been investigated.

articleTitle: Validation of hybrid MoM scheme for composite geometries with layered structures
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this work, the previously developed hybrid MoM scheme with special Green's function is applied to modeling the composite geometries with layered structures. A good matching of simulated results obtained by this approach with direct multi-dielectric MoM approach and with measurements is demonstrated. The computational efficiency of hybrid MoM approach against the direct MoM is concluded.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of large aperture rectenna lattice
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Generalized scheme of large-aperture rectenna laticce is considered. Equation of state for an infinite rectenna lattice is obtained and proved that the calculation of its nonlinear regime is reduced to the calculation of parameters of “equivalent” receiving and rectifying element at fundamental frequency and frequencies of harmonics.

articleTitle: Compact dual-element printed monopole array at 2.6 GHz with application for MIMO terminal
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A compact two-element antenna for multiple input multiple output (MIMO) system integrated in mobile handset operating for 2.6GHz or LTE-2600 is proposed. It consist of L-shape radiator and two folded L-Shape stripes extending from ground plane operating for mobile phone handset. The monopole itself resonates at a high frequency. The electrical length of monopole antenna can be increased by incorporating short stripes (Stripe_1 and Stripe_ 2) near L-Shape monopole. The coupling is helpful in improve impendence matching by reducing the inductive behavior for L-shape monopole. The Simulation results show the antenna performance meet necessary criteria for LTE 2600 or 2.6 GHz with average impedance bandwidth of 220 MHz, peak gain of 2.8 dB and total efficiency of 80 % and −11 dB isolation without using any decoupling network for two antenna structure.

articleTitle: “CO” shape wire antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The antenna structure is presented by two wires, one is arc shaped and another loop shaped. The antenna shape reminds concentrically placed letters “C” and “O” and for simplicity it is called “CO”. The main idea is to get antenna with simple design and directional radiation pattern. The antenna is studied numerically and simulation results are presented and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Examinations of radar reflections from rains near ground surface
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The results of experimental study of the Doppler spectra for radar reflections from moderate rains in mm band of electromagnetic waves near ground surface are presented. The Doppler spectra were examined using the measuring radar device based upon the coherent receive-transmit semiconductor module. Bartlett's periodograms for spectral power density were considered for visual information on Doppler spectra. The main numerical spectral characteristics (the centre frequency and the effective spectral width of the Doppler spectrum) of radar reflections from rains were calculated and analyzed as well.

articleTitle: Kinedynamics of spherical wavefields in fluid and dielectric continua
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Disturbances induced by physical sources in fluids or dielectrics maintain their primary character while propagating throughout either of these bi-dynamic continua. The paper defines and illustrates four sets of bi-fields based on four specific fundamental kinedynamic solutions to inhomogeneous wave equations related to quasi-point acoustic and electromagnetic sources.

articleTitle: Axially symmetric TM-wave radiation from the sphere-conical cavity
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The axially symmetric TM-wave radiation from the sphere-conical cavity resonator is investigated. The problem is solved rigorously using the analytical regularization technique. Resonator is formed by a perfectly conducting semi-infinite truncated cone joined with the spherical diaphragm by which one of conical sectors is closed. The electric radial dipole is placed in front of the aperture. The problem is reduced to an infinite system of linear algebraic equations (ISLAE) of the second kind. The dependence of the resonance modes radiation through the aperture on the geometrical parameters, as well as the features of the formation of far field patterns are investigated.

articleTitle: Study of wave propagation in two-dimensional photonic crystal
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Strict solution of vector integral - differential equation describing electromagnetic wave propagation in photonic crystals was obtained. The crystals include dielectric, semiconductor and thin metallic films. Complex dielectric permittivity of materials in optical diapason is taken into account. The simple method of obtaining complex propagate number in structures with low loss are proposed and proved. Bandgap effects were analyzed in planar photonic crystals composed from new and useful optical materials.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave radiation from flat waveguide with finite number of slots
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Characteristics of the radiation of electromagnetic waves from the flat metallic waveguide filled with a dielectric and having the finite number of non-uniform parallel slots placed on one side of the waveguide excited by a fundamental waveguide wave are studied. This structure allows an accurate electrodynamic solution with minimum familiar radiophysical assumptions and as a model might give good correspondence to real antennas fabricated of thin foiled dielectric having electrically long slots. The problem is solved by the method of analytical semi-inversion of original problem operator in combination with the method of moments. Near and far radiation fields (E and H-field components), and power characteristics of reflected and propagated in the waveguide fields are analyzed also.

articleTitle: Delays of multiple reflections from Bragg layered structures
publicationTitle: 2016 XXIst International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The time delays of pulses reflected from periodic and non-periodic Bragg layered structures have been investigated. The specific structures such as Bragg reflectors and structures with chirp variation of thickness of the “period” have been considered. The calculation has been carried out under the conditions that carrier frequency is in the vicinity of the Bragg resonance values. The parameters of interpolating models have been found by methods Prony and continued fractions.
